devdoc.details: Contract that provides role-based access control and pausing functionality.

AccessControlBadConfirmation().details: The caller of a function is not the expected one. NOTE: Don't confuse with {AccessControlUnauthorizedAccount}.

OwnableUnauthorizedAccount(address).details: The caller account is not authorized to perform an operation.

params.account: The address of the unauthorized account.

Initialized(uint64).details: Triggered when the contract has been initialized or reinitialized.

PausedChange(bytes4,bool).details: Emitted when a method is paused or unpaused.

RoleAdminChanged(bytes32,bytes32,bytes32.details: Emitted when `newAdminRole` is set as ``role``'s admin role, replacing `previousAdminRole` `DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE` is the starting admin for all roles, despite {RoleAdminChanged} not being emitted signaling this.

RoleGranted(bytes32,address,address).details: Emitted when `account` is granted `role`. `sender` is the account that originated the contract call. This account bears the admin role (for the granted role). Expected in cases where the role was granted using the internal {AccessControl-_grantRole}.

RoleRevoked(bytes32,address,address).details: Emitted when `account` is revoked `role`. `sender` is the account that originated the contract call:   - if using `revokeRole`, it is the admin role bearer   - if using `renounceRole`, it is the role bearer (i.e. `account`)

checkRole(bytes32).details: Checks if the caller has a specific role.

getRoleAdmin(bytes32).details: Returns the admin role that controls `role`. See {grantRole} and {revokeRole}. To change a role's admin, use {_setRoleAdmin}.

getRoleMember(bytes32,uint256).details: Returns one of the accounts that have `role`. `index` must be a value between 0 and {getRoleMemberCount}, non-inclusive. Role bearers are not sorted in any particular way, and their ordering may change at any point. WARNING: When using {getRoleMember} and {getRoleMemberCount}, make sure you perform all queries on the same block. See the following https://forum.openzeppelin.com/t/iterating-over-elements-on-enumerableset-in-openzeppelin-contracts/2296[forum post] for more information.

getRoleMemberCount(bytes32).details: Returns the number of accounts that have `role`. Can be used together with {getRoleMember} to enumerate all bearers of a role.

getRoleMembers(bytes32).details: Return all accounts that have `role` WARNING: This operation will copy the entire storage to memory, which can be quite expensive. This is designed to mostly be used by view accessors that are queried without any gas fees. Developers should keep in mind that this function has an unbounded cost, and using it as part of a state-changing function may render the function uncallable if the set grows to a point where copying to memory consumes too much gas to fit in a block.

grantRole(bytes32,address).details: Grants `role` to `account`. If `account` had not been already granted `role`, emits a {RoleGranted} event. Requirements: - the caller must have ``role``'s admin role.

renounceRole(bytes32,address).details: Revokes `role` from the calling account. Roles are often managed via {grantRole} and {revokeRole}: this function's purpose is to provide a mechanism for accounts to lose their privileges if they are compromised (such as when a trusted device is misplaced). If the calling account had been revoked `role`, emits a {RoleRevoked} event. Requirements: - the caller must be `callerConfirmation`. May emit a {RoleRevoked} event.

revokeRole(bytes32,address).details: Revokes `role` from `account`. If `account` had been granted `role`, emits a {RoleRevoked} event. Requirements: - the caller must have ``role``'s admin role.

selectorToPaused(bytes4).details: Gets the paused state for a specific function selector.

setPaused(bytes4,bool).details: Sets the paused state for a specific function selector.

explanation: Static deployed ABI/source inventory plus dated read-only selector observations, not future runtime identity or successful-execution, liquidity, backing or financial-safety assurance. All admitted calls are nonpayable and require zero native value, grants, canonical calldata, balances and independent controls.

Ethereum YelayLiteVault 0x615989F57f6da73C3a1f96a347536941D88e7E0A routes selectors via owner-controlled mapping, not one EIP1967 implementation. Current observed deposit/redeem/migratePosition routes resolve to FundsFacet 0xce0dE4c16cD7734202939BbeB03905cB750c6901 at recorded block. Sourcify does not detect the custom selector routing and reports this custom-router deployment as isProxy:false; verified vault source establishes delegate routing. Future selector upgrades can change behavior.

Underlying getter at the recorded block returned Ethereum 6-decimal USDC 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48. Assets and ERC1155 share amounts are raw units, not human currency amounts or ordinary ERC4626 ERC20 shares. Supply spans project IDs; deposit requires USDC allowance to the vault and an active client project ID; shares are minted to explicit receiver.

Deposit and redeem accrue all positive strategy interest as new project-0 yield shares held by configured YieldExtractor. User project shares principally represent capital; separately distributed yield claims, Merkle proofs and transform/claim paths are not admitted here. Project/client fee distribution is external to this bounded vault-function inventory, not guaranteed automatic compounding to this caller.

Conversion floors assets*totalSupply/totalAssets (initial deposit uses 1:1 units); no min shares, min assets, max loss or deadline argument protects the transaction. A small deposit can mint zero shares. Deposits try configured deposit-queue strategy adapters by delegatecall with fixed deposit(assets,supplement); if none succeeds, underlying is held internally. Callers cannot provide the adapter, supplement or arbitrary payload in admitted functions.

Redeem burns only msg.sender project shares, with no delegated owner argument or operator allowance path; receiver may differ. It computes assets after fee accrual, requires assets > 10 raw underlying units, and tries configured withdrawal queue. WITHDRAW_MARGIN=10 permits up to 10 raw units of shortfall/normalization; insufficient internal funds reverts. Strategy liquidity, queues and valuation can delay or prevent cash exit even though no user cooldown/withdrawal queue is encoded.

migratePosition burns caller shares and mints equal shares in a different active project under the same client; both IDs must be active and different. It does not move cash or bridge chains. Receiver ERC1155 hooks may revert deposits/migrations. No arbitrary multicall, swap, management/role, approval, token-transfer callback or reward-maintenance entry is admitted.

Each user function checks its own selector pause flag; authority can pause individual calls. Strategies/adapters, queues, client/project activation, role holders, YieldExtractor and selector mappings remain mutable. Official current SDK setup says new client activations are not being accepted; this admission covers ordinary existing active-project vault interactions, not new onboarding or legal eligibility.

Yelay is counted once, including former Spool continuity; no legacy Spool vault/deployment is admitted. Current website offers live yield infrastructure and current docs/repository map this vault. No TVL, usage, APY, performance or whole-workflow assurance is made.

selectedFunctions.label: Yelay Deposit USDC into project
warnings: Static deployed ABI/source inventory plus dated read-only selector observations, not future runtime identity or successful-execution, liquidity, backing or financial-safety assurance. All admitted calls are nonpayable and require zero native value, grants, canonical calldata, balances and independent controls.

Ethereum YelayLiteVault 0x615989F57f6da73C3a1f96a347536941D88e7E0A routes selectors via owner-controlled mapping, not one EIP1967 implementation. Current observed deposit/redeem/migratePosition routes resolve to FundsFacet 0xce0dE4c16cD7734202939BbeB03905cB750c6901 at recorded block. Sourcify does not detect the custom selector routing and reports this custom-router deployment as isProxy:false; verified vault source establishes delegate routing. Future selector upgrades can change behavior.

Underlying getter at the recorded block returned Ethereum 6-decimal USDC 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48. Assets and ERC1155 share amounts are raw units, not human currency amounts or ordinary ERC4626 ERC20 shares. Supply spans project IDs; deposit requires USDC allowance to the vault and an active client project ID; shares are minted to explicit receiver.

Deposit and redeem accrue all positive strategy interest as new project-0 yield shares held by configured YieldExtractor. User project shares principally represent capital; separately distributed yield claims, Merkle proofs and transform/claim paths are not admitted here. Project/client fee distribution is external to this bounded vault-function inventory, not guaranteed automatic compounding to this caller.

Conversion floors assets*totalSupply/totalAssets (initial deposit uses 1:1 units); no min shares, min assets, max loss or deadline argument protects the transaction. A small deposit can mint zero shares. Deposits try configured deposit-queue strategy adapters by delegatecall with fixed deposit(assets,supplement); if none succeeds, underlying is held internally. Callers cannot provide the adapter, supplement or arbitrary payload in admitted functions.

Redeem burns only msg.sender project shares, with no delegated owner argument or operator allowance path; receiver may differ. It computes assets after fee accrual, requires assets > 10 raw underlying units, and tries configured withdrawal queue. WITHDRAW_MARGIN=10 permits up to 10 raw units of shortfall/normalization; insufficient internal funds reverts. Strategy liquidity, queues and valuation can delay or prevent cash exit even though no user cooldown/withdrawal queue is encoded.

migratePosition burns caller shares and mints equal shares in a different active project under the same client; both IDs must be active and different. It does not move cash or bridge chains. Receiver ERC1155 hooks may revert deposits/migrations. No arbitrary multicall, swap, management/role, approval, token-transfer callback or reward-maintenance entry is admitted.

Each user function checks its own selector pause flag; authority can pause individual calls. Strategies/adapters, queues, client/project activation, role holders, YieldExtractor and selector mappings remain mutable. Official current SDK setup says new client activations are not being accepted; this admission covers ordinary existing active-project vault interactions, not new onboarding or legal eligibility.

Yelay is counted once, including former Spool continuity; no legacy Spool vault/deployment is admitted. Current website offers live yield infrastructure and current docs/repository map this vault. No TVL, usage, APY, performance or whole-workflow assurance is made.
